investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. The scheduler message (evidence id: failed-check.message) reports two distinct blocking conditions: (1) the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource have Insufficient capacity — meaning the resource quota or the peer-pod provider limit is exhausted — and (2) the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector, which is expected because those nodes are not configured for kata peer-pods. Preemption was also evaluated and found unhelpful, indicating no lower-priority pods were evictable to free the resource. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885: createAgent called with machineType "remote") never received an agent identity or VM id, leaving all four required evidence fields absent and causing the contract validation to fail completely.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both peer-pod-capable nodes: concurrent remote agent workloads or leaked/zombie peer-pod VMs have consumed all available slots, leaving no capacity for new pods.

SECONDARY — peer-pod provider quota or cloud-provider VM limit reached: the underlying peer-pod provider (e.g., cloud VM quota for the peer-pod node pool) may have hit an account-level or region-level limit, causing the Kubernetes device plugin to report zero allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm units.

TERTIARY — peer-pod node pool scaled down or nodes NotReady: if the 2 kata-capable nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or replaced, the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm count would drop to zero cluster-wide.

QUATERNARY — node affinity or selector misconfiguration on the remote-agent pod spec: if the pod's affinity rules were recently tightened, the 4 non-kata nodes might have previously matched but no longer do; however, the 2 Insufficient messages confirm at least 2 nodes were correctly targeted, so this is a lower-probability cause for the affinity side.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable > 0 and used = 0 on both kata-capable nodes, the resource exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a pod spec or admission webhook misconfiguration would become the primary suspect.

If the eval passed on an immediate re-run without any infrastructure change, the failure would be transient (e.g., a briefly held resource released between runs) rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, a shared infrastructure cause would be less likely and a probe-specific issue in the create path would be implicated.

If the scheduler message changed to a different error (e.g., ImagePullBackOff, OOMKilled, or a different resource constraint) on re-run, the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion diagnosis would need to be revised.
If the 2 kata-capable nodes were found to be NotReady or cordoned, the root cause would shift from resource exhaustion to node availability loss.

Add a remote-agent-cleanup eval that detects and reports pods in the Pending or Unknown phase that are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources beyond a configurable TTL, to catch resource leaks before they exhaust capacity.

Extend the remote-agent-create contract to capture a schedulingLatencyMs evidence field so that scheduling delays can be trended over time and a warning threshold can be set independently of the full agent-ready latency.

Add a kata-node-health eval that checks the Ready status and resource capacity of the kata-capable nodes on each run, providing early warning if a node is drained or its peer-pod provider becomes unhealthy.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod creation attempt was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was violated in full.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on all eligible nodes (0/6 nodes available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector). Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two kata-capable nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never completes, and the check returns a failure before any required evidence can be collected. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is currently scoped to this observability eval.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. The scheduler message (evidence id: failed-check.message) reports two distinct blocking conditions: (1) the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource have Insufficient capacity — meaning the resource quota or the peer-pod provider limit is exhausted — and (2) the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector, which is expected because those nodes are not configured for kata peer-pods. Preemption was also evaluated and found unhelpful, indicating no lower-priority pods were evictable to free the resource. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885: createAgent called with machineType "remote") never received an agent identity or VM id, leaving all four required evidence fields absent and causing the contract validation to fail completely.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both peer-pod-capable nodes: concurrent remote agent workloads or leaked/zombie peer-pod VMs have consumed all available slots, leaving no capacity for new pods.

SECONDARY — peer-pod provider quota or cloud-provider VM limit reached: the underlying peer-pod provider (e.g., cloud VM quota for the peer-pod node pool) may have hit an account-level or region-level limit, causing the Kubernetes device plugin to report zero allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm units.

TERTIARY — peer-pod node pool scaled down or nodes NotReady: if the 2 kata-capable nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or replaced, the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm count would drop to zero cluster-wide.

QUATERNARY — node affinity or selector misconfiguration on the remote-agent pod spec: if the pod's affinity rules were recently tightened, the 4 non-kata nodes might have previously matched but no longer do; however, the 2 Insufficient messages confirm at least 2 nodes were correctly targeted, so this is a lower-probability cause for the affinity side.

Because no pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was violated in full.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on all eligible nodes (0/6 nodes available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector). Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two kata-capable nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never completes, and the check returns a failure before any required evidence can be collected. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is currently scoped to this observability eval.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-13T23:48–23:53Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes had insufficient VM capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0/6 nodes available for scheduling. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never received any response evidence, causing all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) to be missing and the check to fail.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on its 2 peer-pod-capable nodes. Every eval attempt to create a remote agent pod timed out unscheduled (~141–146 s) because: (1) both kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm", and (2) the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable on all 6 nodes. This is a cluster-level infrastructure resource exhaustion localized to the remote-agent pod scheduling path, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present; this is an eval infrastructure failure against the production-api environment.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:262-270: contract requires message containsIgnoreCase 'hello from aura' — assertion was never reached because the pod never scheduled
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes satisfy, so even if VM capacity were freed, the 4 other nodes could not accept the pod. This is a configuration constraint, not a capacity issue, but it compounds the exhaustion problem.

TERTIARY — Leaked or stuck remote agent pods from prior eval runs consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them: if cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) failed in a previous run, orphaned pods may be holding VM resources. No direct evidence of leaked pods is present in this packet, but the pattern of all three sequential checks failing suggests the resource was already exhausted before this run began.

LOW PROBABILITY — Cluster node count reduction or node failure reducing the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes below the expected baseline: not supported by direct evidence in this packet but cannot be ruled out without kubectl node inspection.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — eval checks: remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and allocated counts on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes immediately to confirm resource exhaustion and determine how many VM slots are in use vs. available.

Identify and terminate any orphaned or stuck remote agent pods from prior eval runs that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them; verify that the withCleanup() path in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916) is executing correctly on eval completion and failure.

If VM slots are genuinely exhausted by legitimate workloads, evaluate whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 capable nodes needs to be increased, or whether additional peer-pod-capable nodes need to be added to the cluster.

Investigate whether the node affinity/selector configuration on remote agent pods is intentional and correctly scoped; if the 4 non-kata nodes could be made eligible for remote agent pods with a configuration change, this would increase scheduling resilience.

Once cluster capacity is restored, re-run the full remote-agents eval suite to confirm all three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) return to passing status and that the expected evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are present.

Review the degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 thresholds in features.json (lines 187–188) to confirm whether this failure has triggered a feature degraded or outage status signal in the observability dashboard.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together to confirm shared dependency failure
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: If all three fail with the same scheduling message again, it confirms the shared cluster resource is the single point of failure rather than any per-check logic.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (non-zero) kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes at the time of the failure, resource exhaustion would not be the cause and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., a broken admission webhook or a changed resource request value in the pod spec) would need to be investigated.

If the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks passed in a subsequent run without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient capacity spike rather than sustained exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the root cause would be localized to the runtime check's pod spec or configuration rather than a shared cluster capacity problem.

If the pod scheduling error message changed to a different reason (e.g., image pull failure, OOMKilled, or a different resource type) in a re-run, it would indicate the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion was resolved but a different issue emerged.

If no pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (i.e., the resource appears free but scheduling still fails), the node affinity/selector mismatch or a misconfigured resource limit on the pod spec would become the primary hypothesis.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity across all cluster nodes before attempting remote agent creation, and fails fast with a descriptive capacity-exhaustion message rather than waiting for the full pod scheduling timeout (~150 s).
Add an eval that detects and reports orphaned remote agent pods (pods in Pending or Running state older than a configurable threshold) that may be leaking kata.peerpods.io/vm slots between eval runs.

Add a cluster node health eval that verifies the expected number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes are present and reporting non-zero allocatable VM capacity before any remote-agents checks are attempted.

Consider adding a latency-budget warning eval that fires when remote agent pod scheduling exceeds a shorter threshold (e.g., 30 s) to surface capacity pressure earlier than the current 141–150 s timeout observed in this failure.
